summary: Jan–Jun 2026 oil palm yield 7.97 t/ha (2,369.59 t), 2.8% below the same period of 2025 (Agro).
2025 yield 18.07 t/ha, 3% below the 18.61 budget and 11% below 2024's 20.40 (PA).

issues.title: R21 rubber supplying figures conflict
issues.detail: PA 1/2026 (7.1.4): 3,300 trees supplied in 2025 and another 3,000 seedlings needed in 2026. Agro 1/2026 (7.7): 2,700 seedlings supplied in 2025 with 600 points still vacant.

issues.title: R14 rubber yield likely misreported
issues.detail: Agro 1/2026 Table 14 shows R14 at 1,123 kg/ha for Jan–Jun 2026 vs 339 in 2025 (+231.3%), lifting the estate total to 591 kg/ha (+91.3%). The agronomist doubts the data and asked the estate to recheck. PA 1/2026 had R14 at only 507 kg/ha for all of 2025.

issues.title: Year-on-year yield mixes area bases
issues.detail: PA 1/2026 crop table: 2024 total 20.40 t/ha uses 270.53 ha (5,517.66 t per Agro Table 7). The 2025 total of 18.07 t/ha uses 297.36 ha (5,374.76 t), which adds PR21H (26.83 ha at 4.62 t/ha scout yield). So the stated -11.42% partly reflects the larger area base.

issues.title: Block areas in section headings differ from area tables
issues.detail: Agro 1/2026 heads R21 as 27.92 ha and PR21B as 23.07 ha. Its own Table 1 and the PA area statement give R2021 = 20.42 ha and PR2021 H = 26.83 ha.

issues.title: P97/P99 replant timing inconsistent
issues.detail: PA 1/2026 summary table says felling and chipping start in May, but section 2.3 says June (with April recommended) and planting is to finish by Dec 2026. Agro 1/2026 says land preparation started in March 2026 and is now on hold due to the diesel price hike.

issues.title: PR21/H basal pruning deadline differs within PA
issues.detail: PA 1/2026 summary item 14 says basal pruning is to be completed by March 2026; section 7.3.5 says by May 2026 (only 15 ha done by Dec 2025).

issues.title: PA manuring table date error (P2018 G2 RP)
issues.detail: PA 1/2026 Summary of Manuring 2025: P2018 G2 rock phosphate shows actual month 'March' but the remark says 'Completed on August 2025'.

issues.title: PA bunch weight table lists 2004 twice
issues.detail: PA 1/2026 6.1.9 lists planting years 2001, 2004, 2004, 2013, 2018. The second '2004' row (22.1 kg to 20.3 kg) is presumably 2005.

issues.title: P18 age-profile share does not reconcile
issues.detail: Agro 1/2026 2.4 says prime-age palms rose to 26.8% with P18. On the same planted-area basis used for P21 (8.3%) and P23 (8.5%), P18's 72.55 ha is 22.3% of 324.88 ha. Its census palms (8,591 of 35,731) are 24.0%.

issues.title: Census table subtotals off
issues.detail: Agro 1/2026 Table 2: P2005 sub-blocks 10.60 + 21.42 = 32.02 ha but the subtotal shows 32.05. The block subtotals sum to 346.11 ha vs a grand total of 346.08 ha.

issues.title: Wrong block / unit labels in Agro report
issues.detail: Agro 1/2026 8.8 cites extended intervals in 'P97, P98 and P13', but Beranang has no P98 (likely P99). Appendix 1(e) is headed KG/PALM for R21 compound at 250, which can only be grams.

issues.title: P13 yield: under 5 t/ha or 6.74?
issues.detail: Agro 1/2026 4.1.2 says little crop (<5 mt/ha) was recovered from P97, P99 and P13 to date, but Table 13 and 8.4 give P13 at 6.74 t/ha for Jan–Jun 2026 ('less than 7 mt/ha').

issues.title: Rubber area base differs in Agro Table 14
issues.detail: Agro 1/2026 Table 14 uses 2025 areas of 35.1, 20.0 and 33.0 ha (88.1 total) but 33.15, 17.60 and 32.98 ha (83.73) for 2026; PA 1/2026 area statement gives mature rubber 83.73 ha.

actions.item: Recruit harvesters, sprayers, manurers and tappers; find root cause of high worker turnover
Keep harvesting intervals at 15 days or less and collect all loose fruit (P97, P99, P01, P05, P13)
Raise harvester output to 3 t/manday in 2001, 2004 and 2005 plantings
Start a formal Ganoderma census and keep deboling fallen palms
Bring outstanding 2026 fertiliser rounds up to date (oil palm and rubber)
Apply the overdue extra kieserite round in PR21B (prescribed March 2026)
Clear pruning backlogs in P04 and P13; continue progressive pruning in P01/P04/P05
Complete basal pruning in PR21/H and PR23 (scout harvesting started May 2026)
Verify vacant points and supply PR23 (150 palms) and R21 vacancies
Build proper terraces in hilly P97/P99 replant
Expedite weeding: VOPs/Asystasia in mature blocks, circles in P18, PR21B, PR23, R14 and R21
Recheck R14 rubber yield records; collect latex weekly to stop overflow
Improve tapping standard: depth, monthly spot marking, double-tapping for vacant tasks, annual brown bast census
Prune side shoots in R21 up to 3.0 m; do annual girth measurement
Half-yearly single rat baiting in P18; improve drainage in its low-lying areas
Keep cattle out of PR21B and immature areas
Resolve road grading: only 193.97 of 1,200 chains graded; contractor stopped over low rates

kb:
LADANG SUNGAI BERANANG (Inisiatif Jaya Sdn Bhd; Far East Holdings Berhad on the Agronomy cover; Prosper group). Plantation Controller Dr. Chua Chin Kok. Senior Manager En. Zulkarnain Bin Barik. Mr. Muruganathan A/L Arumugam is called Senior Assistant In-Charge in the PA report and Manager in the Agronomy report. Planting Advisor Mr. Boey Chee Weng. Agronomist Mr. Chong Kuan Ming.
Sources: PA Report 1/2026 (visit 20 Feb 2026, reviews Jan-Dec 2025). Agronomy Report 1/2026 (visit 25 Jun 2026, previous visit 17 Dec 2025).

AREA (PA 1/2026, as at Dec 2025). Oil palm mature: P1997 A 37.64 ha, P1999 B 40.87, P2001 C 26.09, P2004 D 46.94, P2005 E 32.02, P2013 F 14.42, P2018 G1 17.52, G2 27.31, G3 27.72. Total mature 270.53 ha. Immature: PM2021 H 26.83 and PR2023 I 27.52, total 54.35 ha. Total oil palm 324.88 ha. Rubber: mature R2006 33.15, R2007 17.60, R2014 32.98 (83.73 ha); immature R2021 20.42 ha; total rubber 104.15 ha. Other land 87.99 ha: vacant ex-mining Phase 3 13.69, building sites 3.44, nursery and pond 0.52, unsuitable 21.07, TNB reserves 38.87, JKR road 10.40. Total estate 517.02 ha. PR21/H became mature from January 2026, so mature oil palm in 2026 is 297.36 ha (Agro yield table). P97/A and P99/B are scheduled for replanting in 2026 with seedlings from Kemayan Estate. There are no 2027 replanting plans (PA). Agro 1/2026: land preparation started March 2026 but is on hold due to the diesel price hike; terraces are essential on the steep terrain.
Age profile (Agro): over 50% of palms are older than 20 years; 24.2% are older than 25 and due for replanting. P18 is now prime age (stated as 26.8%), P21 is 8.3% and P23 is 8.5% of planted area.
Palm census by PARAS GIS drone (Agro Table 2, 2026). Stand per hectare (SPH) by block: P97 110 (4,017 palms, 36.64 ha); P99 76 (3,294, 43.58 ha); P01 106 (C1 111, C2 101); P04 126 (6,328 palms, 50.13 ha); P05 111 (E1 128, E2 93); P13 70 (F1 68, F2 97); P18 115 (G1 120, G2 117, G3 111); P21H 102 (2,724 palms); PR23 90 (2,794 palms, 31.00 ha). Grand total 35,731 palms on 346.08 drone ha, 103 SPH. SPH is below 100 in P99, P05E2, P13F1, P13F2 and P23; verify vacant points and supply.

LABOUR (PA, Dec 2025). Oil palm (requirement vs actual): harvesters 19 vs 10 (short 9; actual ratio 1:27 ha against 1:14 ha required); manurers 5 vs 3; sprayers 6 vs 2; general workers 2 vs 3; office cleaner 1/1; security 2/2; drivers 2/2. Total 37 required, 23 actual, short 14. Workers to planted area 1:14 ha. Rubber: tappers 16 vs 11 (short 5); driver 1/1; mandore 1/1; total 18 vs 13. A tapping contractor is waiting on Resident Directors' approval because it wants higher rates. High worker turnover is the main issue. Staff (6) are adequate, with no changes.

UPKEEP 2025 (PA). Oil palm circle spraying: 369.04 of 700.58 ha (53%, 1.4 of 2.5 rounds), held back by the sprayer shortage. Circles are clean. Output 3.9 ha/manday, RM18/ha, earnings RM70.20/day, glyphosate 0.81 L/ha. Selective spraying: 673.83 of 884.14 ha (76%). VOPs, lalang and Asystasia remain. Mist blower 4.6 ha/manday, RM18/ha, earnings RM82.80/day, Garlon 0.4 L/ha (advised to use Garlon only, without Ally). A neglected plot in P13/F now has a new access road. Rubber strip spraying: 200.61 of 251.19 ha (80%), 4.4 ha/manday. Rubber selective spraying: 134.48 of 167.46 ha (80%), 3.8 ha/manday (low; 5 is possible); use Garlon on hard woodies in R07.
Manuring 2025 (PA): oil palm 32 of 32 rounds (100%). Wheelbarrow output was 20 bags/manday against an expected 25-30, at RM2.40/bag and RM48/day. Sub-surface application in P01/C (NK mixture 23.25 t) and P05/E (MIX B 34.60 t) at 15 bags/manday and RM4.80/bag. Rubber: 6 of 6 rounds, 53.30 t applied (100%).
Agro 1/2026: all 2025 programmes were done, some late. As of June 2026 the outstanding oil palm rounds are: MIX B in P05E (Feb), P04D (Apr), P13F (Jan and Apr), P18G (May) and P21H (May); RP in P04D, P05E and P13F (May); kieserite in P13F (Feb), P18G (Mar) and P21H (Mar). Outstanding rubber rounds: R06 (Mar), R07 (Feb), R14 (Jan), R21 (Jan and Apr). The delays are due to labour shortage. Fertiliser delivery, quality and storage are fine.
Pruning 2025 (PA): 579.76 of 1,082.12 ha progressively pruned (54%), held back by the harvester shortage. P05 and P04 were delayed, with fractured fronds in P04. Cost per palm per year is RM1.20 (2001/2004/2005) and RM0.70 (2013/2018). Agro (June 2026): P97/P99 pruning is pending; P01 and P05 are up to date; P04 has localised under-pruning; P13 corrective pruning is progressing; PR21B is 56% complete.
Weeding 2026 (Agro): only 1 round of inter-row weeding in P01, P04 and P05, and 1 circle round in P97, P99, P05 and P13. VOPs in circles in P01, P04 and P05. Mucuna is encroaching into paths in P13 terraces. Weeding in P97/P99 should be skipped if the replant proceeds.
Roads (PA): 193.97 of 1,200 chains graded at RM10/chain; the contractor stopped over low rates. A backhoe was used for 1,186 of 1,250 hours at RM50/hour for patching. Drains: 100 chains budgeted at RM35, not done and not needed.
Pests and diseases: rat damage census for 2025 (PA) was 1.9-4.9% (quarterly, fresh attack per palm). One baiting round with Storm in P18 G1/G2 (Oct 2025); bait if damage exceeds 10%. Agro rat census for 2026: Q1 2.2-4.1%, Q2 2.4-4.6%; leaf-eating pests at 0%. Ganoderma is in P01, P05 and P18 (PA) and mainly in P01 and P05 (Agro). There has been no formal census, only ad hoc deboling, and both reports ask for a census.

CROP 2025 (PA). Oil palm yield in t/ha, 2024 vs 2025: P97 14.91 to 10.61 (-28.84%); P99 14.61 to 10.37 (-29.02%); P01 27.32 to 23.13; P04 24.70 to 22.77; P05 25.49 to 21.65; P13 12.37 to 11.49; G1 22.85 to 27.79; G2 20.12 to 25.45; G3 19.58 to 25.76; PN2021 H 0 to 4.62. Total 20.40 to 18.07 (-11.42%). Budget was 18.61 t/ha (3% shortfall), mainly due to the harvester shortage. Harvesting rounds were 19 vs a budget of 24, and the average interval was 23 days. One Badang (3 cutters and 1 collector) works the flat areas. Harvesting rates are RM37-50/t for mature blocks and RM90/t for P21H. Output was 1.50-2.68 t/manday in the mature blocks (0.59 in PN2021 H), with a target of 3 t/manday for the 2001/2004/2005 plantings. Basic wage is RM65.39. Bunch weights fell for the older plantings (e.g. 2001: 22.6 to 21.7 kg), possibly from harvesting over-ripe bunches.
Monthly FFB production (Agro Table 7): 2024 total 5,517.66 t; 2025 total 5,374.76 t; 2026 Jan-Jun 401.62, 362.80, 396.91, 377.75, 431.73, 398.78, totalling 2,369.59 t.
Yield Jan-Jun (Agro Table 13), 2025 vs 2026 in t/ha: P97 6.08 to 2.95 (-51.5%); P99 5.89 to 3.04 (-48.4%); P01 9.12 to 11.73 (+28.6%); P04 9.55 to 10.14; P05 8.87 to 10.84; P13 5.26 to 6.74; P18G1 12.28 to 10.57; G2 11.97 to 10.77; G3 11.71 to 10.29; P21H 2.09 to 5.36. Total (297.36 ha) 8.20 to 7.97 (-2.8%). Most fields had fewer than the minimum target of 12 rounds in Jan-Jun 2026; Agro 8.8 names P97, 'P98' (no such block, probably P99) and P13 as having fewer than 8 rounds.
Harvesting intervals Jan-May 2026 (Agro Table 8): P97 19-26 days, P99 19-27, P01 11-24, P04 13-23, P05 13-24, P13 14-24. P18 12-19 (Table 12, Jan-Jun 2026). P21H up to 21 days. Target is 15 days or less.
Rubber (PA): 2025 yield 611 kg/ha vs a budget of 982 (38% below) and 927 in 2024 (-34%). Output 22 kg per tapper vs a budget of 25. There was no stimulant on R06/R07 and tapping quality is poor (panel wounding, inconsistent spot marking). Contract rates are latex RM2/kg and scrap RM1.20/kg. Agro Jan-Jun 2026: R06 247 kg/ha, R07 242, R14 1,123 (+231%, data under verification), total 591. Tapper turnout was 81.3% (1,073 of 1,320). Latex overflow in R14 comes from biweekly collection, so collect weekly. There has been no weeding in R14.

YOUNG MATURE AND IMMATURE. P18 (Agro): satisfactory, with less Mg deficiency. Pale palms grow in low-lying waterlogged spots (drainage needed). Circles are overgrown with Ageratum and there is mild rat damage. PR21/H (PA): 6 of 6 circle and selective rounds and 5 of 5 fertiliser rounds; 2025 scout yield 4.6 t/ha; basal pruning only 15 ha done (to finish by May 2026). PR21B (Agro): Mg deficiency; extra kieserite from March not applied; weedy with wild brinjal; cattle damage. PR23 (PA): circle 67%, selective 33% (lalang), fertiliser 5 of 5 rounds, good fruit set, 150 palms to supply. Agro: about 29 months old; scout harvesting started May 2026; basal pruning to do; Clidemia, Hedyotis, Tetracera and lalang present. R21 rubber: strip and selective 50% (PA), fertiliser 4 of 4 rounds. Supplying figures conflict: PA says 3,300 supplied in 2025 and 3,000 more needed; Agro says 2,700 supplied and 600 vacant. Trunk size is small and variable, so maturity will be deferred. Side shoots need pruning.

FERTILISER 2026 (Agro Appendix 1, revised), g per palm:
P01: NK1 7000 sub-surface in Jan.
P04: MIX B 2250 Jan, MIX B 2000 Apr, RP 1500 May, MIX B 2250 Aug.
P05: MIX B 8000 sub-surface in Feb, RP 1500 May.
P13: MIX B 2000 Jan, KIE 1000 Feb, MIX B 2000 Apr, RP 1750 May, MIX B 2000 Aug.
P18: MIX B 2250 Feb and May, KIE 750 Mar, RP 2000 Jul, MIX B 1500 Aug and Nov.
PR21B: MIX B 1500 Feb, May, Aug and Nov; KIE 500 Mar; RP 2000 Jul.
PR23C: same as PR21B without the KIE.
P97/P99 replant: CRF 600 and RP 500 per planting hole.
Rubber compound 10-12-13-2: R06 550 Mar and Sep; R07 600 Feb and Aug; R14 650 Jan and Jul. R21 compound 14-13-9-2.5 at 250 in Jan, Apr, Jul and Oct.
The 2027 programme follows the second agronomy visit.

RAINFALL (Agro Appendix 2), mm and rain days: 2020 2,533 (163); 2021 2,464 (157); 2022 3,821 (169); 2023 2,819 (117); 2024 2,519 (146); 2025 2,441 (128).

DATA ISSUES: R21 supply figures conflict between the reports. R14 rubber yield is suspect. The 2024 vs 2025 yield uses different area bases. Agro section headings give PR21B as 23.07 ha and R21 as 27.92 ha against 26.83 and 20.42 in the area tables. Replant and basal pruning deadlines are inconsistent within the PA report. The PA manuring table has a G2 RP date error and the bunch-weight table lists 2004 twice. The Agro text cites a non-existent P98, and the R21 dose unit is wrong. Agro 4.1.2 says under 5 t/ha from P13 to date but Table 13 and 8.4 give 6.74 t/ha. Agro Table 14 uses 2025 rubber areas of 35.1, 20.0 and 33.0 ha (88.1 total) against 33.15, 17.60 and 32.98 ha (83.73) for 2026.

ffbProd.monthlySrc: Agronomy Report 1/2026 (visit 25 Jun 2026) Table 7 Monthly Production, whole estate (MT). Printed totals 5,517.66 / 5,374.76 / 2,369.59 all equal the sum of the printed months.
ffbProd.notes: Only Agro 1/2026 prints tonnes; PA 1/2026, PA/Agro 2-2025, 1-2025, 2-2024 print yield in t/ha only (no FFB tonnage; 2-2024 has a production chart that is not readable as text). So only 2024 and 2025 full-year tonnages exist. 2025 oil palm yield printed 18.07 t/ha (PA 1/2026, 270.53 ha mature + 26.83 ha PM21H = 297.36 ha implied) and 19.44 t/ha (Agro 2-2025, 270.53 ha mature only, before P21H) - basis differs. Estate area includes mature oil palm only; rubber not included. Jan-Jun 2026 yield 7.97 t/ha on 297.36 ha (Agro Table 13). No 2026 data after June.
